clue.text: Account holder has son to maintain

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: A bank customer keeps a son's account going.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps money in a deposit account at a bank is a saver.

clue.text: Way to set up motorists' travel agency in USA

parts.note: a street is a way or road

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the piece is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A road is planned for a motoring club's travel firm in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns RAC into CAR. 'Travel agency' looks like a booking firm, but agency here means a means of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: An American tram, a rail vehicle running on city roads, moves people about.

clue.text: It is abandoned by caller for face-saving purposes

indicators.note: is abandoned by means these letters are dropped from the caller word

parts.note: a visitor is someone who calls
taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone caller drops a topic to save face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-saving' suggests avoiding embarrassment; the shield literally protects the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet's movable front shield or a peaked cap's brim guards the eyes and skin.

clue.text: Revised itinerary — engineers arranging detour

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: arranging means the letters of the next word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Army engineers set up a detour, so the trip plan changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey sent a different way has had its planned route altered.

clue.text: Dark horse at twenty to one possibly causing an upset

definitions.text: Dark horse at twenty to one possibly
definitions.meaning: a mare out at twenty to one in the morning is a horse at night
something deeply upsetting, a bad experience that disturbs

explanation.surface: An outsider at long odds in a race might cause a shock result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twenty to one' looks like betting odds, but it is also the time 12.40am, so the horse is out in the dark. The second sense is the bad dream or ordeal that upsets you.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare after dark is literally a female horse at night, and a distressing ordeal is likened to a bad dream.

clue.text: Upright fellow

annotationWithheld.why: Upright fellow (4) for NEIL: no parse found; NEIL is a man's name but nothing in 'Upright' gives it, and its reversal LIEN is not a fellow

clue.text: Dismissive instruction to firefighters?

parts.note: a rude brush-off phrase, read literally as an order sending fire crews to the flames

explanation.definitionFit: An irritated way of telling someone to clear off, read literally as an order to attend fires.

clue.text: Pickwickian put up on island

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word put is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: taken as written
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is lodged on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracy Tupman is a member of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupman is one of Mr Pickwick's companions in Dickens's novel.

clue.text: Cause of current build-up if one is put in wide river

indicators.note: is put in means these letters go inside the word for wide

parts.note: ample means wide or roomy
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A broad river swells if one stream joins it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests a river's flow, but it is electric current boosted by the device.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic device boosts the strength of a signal or electrical current.

clue.text: Always poetical — that's strange

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A poetic 'always' strikes someone as odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncanny or weird gives a spooky feeling.

clue.text: No action required about coach reservation

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: rest is a period with no action
a coach is a railway carriage, part of a train

explanation.surface: A notice says no further action is needed regarding a coach seat booking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' looks like a booking, but it is the definition in the sense of holding back, as in 'without reservation'; 'about' is the container signal, and 'required' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back one's feelings or opinions is self-control, the reserve meant by 'with reservation'.

clue.text: Standard exercise included in examination

indicators.note: included in means the exercise piece sits inside the standard piece

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A routine physical drill forms part of a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is often called a paper, the set of written questions sat by candidates.

clue.text: With the head away, afraid to give a severe reprimand

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken away here

parts.note: fearful means afraid

explanation.surface: Someone frightened, with their boss absent, gives a harsh telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A long scolding is something you get an earful of, a tongue-lashing.

clue.text: A case is essential back in Lincoln

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the name of the president

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's familiar name

indicators.note: back says the word for essential is read from right to left

parts.note: vital means essential

explanation.surface: A legal case is vital again in Lincoln, the English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns VITAL into LATIV, which goes 'in' ABE. Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city but is the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is one of the noun cases, expressing means or separation.

clue.text: Change into a later fashion

indicators.note: fashion used as a verb means to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Switch to a more recent style of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A modification or adjustment is a change.

clue.text: Crash start by new driver on other side of junction

indicators.note: start means just the first letter of the word Crash is used

parts.note: L is the learner plate shown by a new driver in Britain
overleaf means on the other side of the page

explanation.surface: A novice motorist crashes on the far side of a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a road accident; in fact the junction is the definition and 'on other side' is the page sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway interchange with looping slip roads, shaped like a four-leaved plant, is called this.

clue.text: Parcel post never made a loss

indicators.note: to parcel out is to divide up, so the letters are split and redistributed

explanation.surface: A postal service never turned a profit on parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parcel post' reads as a service; 'Parcel' is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending beyond one's budget leaves a deficit.

clue.text: Runner unfit after finish of canter

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first
finish of means just the last letter of the word canter

parts.note: ill means unwell, unfit

explanation.surface: A racehorse is in poor shape after the end of a gentle canter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like a horse; it is a stream, water that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brook or stream is a runner in crossword terms because water runs.

clue.text: Freemasons, perhaps, on square footing

parts.note: Freemasons meet in lodges, so they are lodge men
a T-square is the drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Masons are on a level footing, as their square symbol suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A foothold or secure position gained is a lodgement.

clue.text: Former pupil, the only one Lawrence dated

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school
sole means the only one
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: An old boy recalls that Lawrence dated only one girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' reads as a verb of courting, but it is the adjective meaning out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date is no longer in use, outmoded.

clue.text: Was sorry, for being rough, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and we take its sound

parts.note: rude can mean rough or crude

explanation.surface: Someone apologised for having been rough.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to have felt sorry about it.

clue.text: One of the team in the long grass is called back

indicators.note: in puts the team player inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
a member is one of a team

explanation.surface: A fielder searching for the ball in the long grass is recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Called back' looks like a summons, but it means recalled to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something to mind is to have it come back into memory.

clue.text: Fat monarch found in food store

parts.note: lard is pig fat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An overweight king is discovered in the pantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or cool cupboard is where food is kept.

clue.text: Selkirk perhaps found here? No, elsewhere

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
not here but elsewhere means away

explanation.surface: Is the sailor Selkirk to be found here? No, somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Selkirk was the Scottish sailor marooned on an island, the model for Robinson Crusoe. 'found' looks like a past tense but is the verb for casting metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Selkirk was a marooned sailor, left alone on an island for four years.

clue.text: Turned up in support of shy creature

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: coy means shy

indicators.note: turned means the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone shy showed up in support of a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' makes PU from UP, placed under COY.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American water rodent is a beast, a creature.

clue.text: Source material used for study programme

indicators.note: material, as raw stuff to be worked up, signals the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Original documents are used for a syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of lessons or lectures on a subject is a programme of study.

clue.text: Rear gunner is superior to enemy initially

indicators.note: superior to means above, so in a down clue these pieces come before

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word enemy

explanation.surface: The tail gunner of a bomber outclasses the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear gunner' reads as one crew member; 'Rear' is the verb, to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up children, or lift up, is to raise them.

clue.text: Weapon mounted in deep emplacement

indicators.note: mounted says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words deep emplacement

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gun is mounted in a deep emplacement.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden run no signal; 'in' is that indicator. 'mounted' in a down clue reads the run upwards, turning EEPE round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing sword is a weapon.

clue.text: Submit a return

definitions.meaning: the profit or output produced, as an investment's annual gain

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both giving way to pressure and the income an investment produces.

clue.text: I am: to introduce summary note? That's not quite accurate

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a precis is a summary
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether to start with a summary note, then admits it is not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague or inexact falls short of being accurate.

clue.text: Pronouncement from Church after extreme article

indicators.note: after says the Church piece follows the other pieces

parts.note: utter means complete or extreme
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A statement issued by the Church after an extreme newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken aloud or declared is a statement or saying.

clue.text: Put up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A defendant is brought up in front of a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To build or raise a structure is to construct it.
